Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: Unit 2. Routine and fun
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Where do real heroes work?
- Materials: Job cards, workplace pictures, career-fair badges, COSYmanuals 'articles' and 'present simple' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• use indefinite articles a/an with occupations
• describe essential community workplaces

Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

teacher — a person who helps students learn. Example: She is my English teacher.
doctor — a person who helps sick people. Example: The doctor works in a hospital.
nurse — a person who cares for sick people. Example: The nurse works in a hospital.
engineer — a person who designs or builds things. Example: He is an engineer.
manager — a person who leads a team. Example: The manager has a meeting.
hospital — a place for medical care. Example: A doctor works in a hospital.
office — a place where people work. Example: I work in an office.
company — a business organisation. Example: She works for a big company.
job — the work you do for money. Example: What is your job?
hero — a person people admire. Example: Nurses are real heroes.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• A doctor works in a hospital. (describing a job and workplace)
• A teacher works in a school. (describing a job and workplace)
• A nurse helps people. (describing a role)
• An engineer works for a company. (describing a job)
• What does a ... do? (asking about a job)
• Real heroes help people. (describing community heroes)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a person who helps students learn'?
Which word means 'a person who helps sick people'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'a/an' for one non-specific countable noun and 'the' for a specific noun.

Form:
Articles: a / an / the: a + consonant sound (a teacher), an + vowel sound (an engineer), the + specific noun (the teacher in our class).

Examples:
• She is a teacher.
• He is an engineer.
• The teacher is in the classroom.
• I have a book and an apple.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
My mother is ___ nurse.
He is ___ engineer.
___ doctor in our town is very kind.
I have ___ apple and ___ banana.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• She is a ... (teacher / doctor / manager).
• He is an ... (engineer / actor / artist).
• The ... is ...
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What is your job or dream job?
• Who is a hero in your community?
• Where does a nurse work?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about jobs with 'a' and 'an'.
• Write three sentences about people in your community with 'the'.
Reading: Where do real heroes work?

Real heroes work in our community. A doctor works in a hospital. A nurse helps people every day. A teacher works in a school. An engineer works for a company. A manager works in an office. These people do important jobs. They are real heroes. What do you do? Where do you work?
Where does a doctor work?
Who works for a company?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What does your mother do?
B: She is a nurse. She works in a hospital.
A: And your father?
B: He is an engineer. He works for a big company.
A: What about you?
B: I am a teacher. I work in a school.
Where does the mother work?
What is the father's job?
Speaking task: Ask your partner about three jobs and workplaces. Use 'a/an' correctly.

• What is your job?
• Where does a nurse work?
• Who is a hero in your community?
• What job do you want?
• Which jobs help people most?
Role-play: You are at a career fair. Talk to three professionals and ask about their jobs.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about jobs and workplaces using 'a/an'.
Model: A ... works in ... An ... works for ...
